grammar.label: modal perfects for deduction about the past
grammar.form: must / can't / could / might / may + have + past participle
grammar.meaning: how certain the speaker is about something that is already over

explanation.en: 'Must have' is near-certainty, 'can't have' is near-impossibility, and 'might/may/could have' sit in the middle. The negative of 'must have' is 'can't have', never 'mustn't have': 'She can't have known — she was abroad.'
explanation.uz: 'must have' — deyarli aniq, 'can't have' — deyarli imkonsiz, 'might/may/could have' — o'rtada. 'must have' ning inkori 'can't have', 'mustn't have' emas.

grammar.positive_example: The lights are off, so they must have gone home.
grammar.negative_example: The lights are off, so they mustn't have gone home.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida taxmin '-sa kerak' qo'shimchasi bilan beriladi va ishonch darajasi ohang bilan ajratiladi; ingliz tilida esa modal fe'l tanlovi bu farqni ko'rsatadi.

grammar.label: degrees of likelihood — be bound to, be likely to, may well
grammar.form: be bound / certain / likely / unlikely + to-infinitive; may well + base verb
grammar.meaning: a scale of expectation, from near-certain to improbable

explanation.en: 'Bound to' is the strongest ('It is bound to rain'), 'likely to' is a fair bet, 'may well' concedes a real chance, and 'unlikely to' pushes it away. All take a to-infinitive except 'may well', which takes the base verb.
explanation.uz: 'bound to' — eng kuchli, 'likely to' — ehtimoldan yiroq emas, 'may well' — haqiqiy imkoniyat, 'unlikely to' — kam ehtimol. 'may well' dan boshqasi 'to' bilan keladi.

grammar.positive_example: Costs are likely to rise again next year.
grammar.negative_example: Costs are likely rise again next year.

l1_notes.uz: 'likely' sifat, shuning uchun 'be' fe'li bilan keladi; uni ravish deb o'ylab 'It likely rains' deyish keng tarqalgan xato.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Careful. 'Two are left' is a conclusion, and I only have a pattern.

body.text: What is likely to happen now?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: An audit. It is bound to find something, though probably not what we expect.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Then I may well have been wrong, and I will say so in writing.
